title: Fish, Rice, and a Clever Way to Fight Parasitic Worms
hook: Farmers in Senegal are adding fish to their rice paddies — and the fish do triple duty: fertilizing the crop, feeding the family, and eating the snails that spread a dangerous parasitic worm.
key_points: Farmers in Senegal are introducing fish into flooded rice paddies alongside the rice crop.
The fish fertilize the paddies and provide an extra source of food for farming families.
The fish also eat the freshwater snails that carry a parasitic worm disease common in the region.
It's a low-cost example of using one intervention — fish farming — to solve food, income, and disease problems at once.
content_html: In parts of Senegal, flooded rice paddies double as a home for a snail that carries a parasitic worm disease — a common hazard for farmers wading through the water. NPR reports that some farmers have found a strikingly simple fix: adding fish to the paddies alongside the rice.
extra_html: The fish earn their keep three times over. They fertilize the rice crop with their waste, they're a source of food and income for farming families, and — crucially — they eat the freshwater snails that host the parasite, cutting down the risk of infection for people working the fields. It's a neat example of a "one-health" approach: instead of treating farming, nutrition, and disease control as separate problems each needing their own program, one low-cost change addresses all three at once.

flashcards.prompt: Why are Senegalese farmers adding fish to their rice paddies?
flashcards.back_html: The fish serve three purposes: fertilizing the rice crop, adding a source of food, and eating the freshwater snails that carry a parasitic worm disease.

flashcards.prompt: What role do the freshwater snails play in this story?

choices.text: They carry a parasitic worm disease that the fish help control by eating them
They're the main food source the fish are farmed to produce
They fertilize the rice paddies directly

flashcards.explanation_html: The snails are the disease risk in this story — they host the parasite. Fish that eat the snails cut down that risk while also fertilizing the paddy and feeding people.
